picked.t: 빈그룹 총수, 빈패스트에 4.4억 달러 추가 투자…우선주 매입
picked.body: 팜 녓 브엉 빈그룹 창업자 겸 회장. (사진=빈그룹) 베트남 최대 민간기업 빈그룹(Vingroup)을 이끄는 팜 녓 브엉(Pham Nhat Vuong) 회장이 4억3,600만 달러 규모 우선주 매입으로 빈패스트(VinFast)에 대한 추가 투자에 나선 것으로 나타났다. 빈패스트가 최근 미국 증권거래위원회(SEC)에 제출한 자료에 따르면, 브엉 회장은 우선주 매입을 통해 빈패스트베트남에 4억3,600만 달러를 추가 투자했다. 빈패스트베트남이 브엉 회장에게 발행한 주식은 전환권 없는 배당 우선주다. 우선주는 일반 주주보다 배당을 먼저, 더 많이 받을 수 있으나, 의결권이 제한되는 것이 일반적이다. 이에 대해 빈패스트는 “브엉 회장의 이번 투자는 당사의 성장을 뒷받침하기 위한 것”이라고 설명했다. 앞서 베트남 증권사 중 하나인 비엣캡증권(Vietcap)은 지난달 21일 빈패스트가 주최한 투자자 간담회 이후 분석을 통해 빈패스트베트남이 해당 자금을 통해 ‘올림픽응옥호이(Olympic Ngoc Hoi)’ 프로젝트의 합작 투자사인 응옥호이부동산을 인수할 가능성이 있다고 전망한 바 있다. 해당 프로젝트는 총 9,171헥타르에 걸쳐 925조7,000억 동(358억7,490만여 달러)이 투자될 예정이다. 빈패스트의 초소형 전기차 VF3. 비엣캡증권에 따르면, 브엉 회장은 2분기 말 기준 빈패스트베트남의 모기업인 빈패스트에 약 40조5,000억 동(약 15억6,960만 달러)을 추가로 투자했다. 앞서 브엉 회장은 “가진 돈이 모두 바닥날 때까지 빈패스트에 대한 투자를 지속할 것”이라고 밝히기도 했다. 브엉 회장은 370억 달러가 넘는 순자산으로 동남아 최대 부호에 올라있다. 그는 빈그룹과 개인 회사를 통해 빈패스트의 지배지분을 확보하고 있다. 자본금 35조 동의 빈패스트베트남은 지난 6월 모기업의 계열 분리를 통해 제조 부문을 제3자에게 위탁하며 설립됐다. 계열 분리 이후, 빈패스트베트남은 빈패스트커머셜&서비스트레이딩(VinFast Commercial & Services Trading LLC), 빈패스트엔지니어링오스트레일리아(VinFast Engineering Australia Pty Ltd), 빈패스트독일(VinFast Germany GmbH) 등의 모든 지분을 보유하며, △전 세계 제품 연구개발(R&D) △A/S △판매 사업을 담당한다.

picked.t: Vietnam must be more strategically proactive amid global uncertainty: PM
picked.body: Vietnam must take a more proactive strategic approach, strengthen domestic capabilities, and expand international cooperation as global economic and geopolitical uncertainties intensify, PM Hung said. Speaking at a dialogue with World Economic Forum (WEF) CEO Stephan Mergenthaler during the 2026 Autumn Economic Forum in HCMC on Oct. 28, Hung outlined Vietnam's response to global economic shifts and its development ambitions for the next decade. The 60-minute dialogue was a highlight of the forum. Mergenthaler opened by asking how Vietnam viewed global changes and their implications for the country's development. The Vietnamese leader said the world was undergoing profound changes, with shifts in the balance of power accelerating the emergence of a more multipolar international order. Strategic competition among major powers is intensifying and extending into economics, technology, data, energy, and standards governing trade, investment, the environment, and governance. Globalization is continuing but becoming more fragmented, with greater emphasis on security, self-reliance, and resilience. Meanwhile, rapid advances in science, technology, and artificial intelligence are transforming production, governance, and the distribution of economic advantages and development resources. These changes pose major challenges, including the need to update international institutions and rules, declining strategic trust amid intensifying competition, and the diminishing effectiveness of traditional growth models, particularly in developing economies. Vietnam therefore needs to strengthen its resilience, strategic autonomy, and capacity to generate new sources of growth, Hung said. "The more uncertain the world becomes, the more strategically proactive Vietnam must be, strengthening its internal capabilities and expanding cooperation," he said. "Vietnam will continue to be a friend, a reliable partner, and a responsible member of the international community, as well as a stable and safe destination for partners and investors." Five priorities to strengthen economic resilience Asked how Vietnam would improve its resilience, Hung outlined five priorities. The first is maintaining political and social stability while strengthening macroeconomic fundamentals, which he described as essential to sustaining confidence among citizens and domestic and foreign businesses. Vietnam will continue to manage macroeconomic policies flexibly to maintain stability, major economic balances, energy security, and food security. Public debt currently stands at around 34% of GDP, giving the country fiscal room to support households and businesses during economic shocks while continuing to invest in strategic infrastructure and development priorities, he said. The second priority is institutional reform, including aligning the legal framework with international standards and practices and removing barriers to business and investment. Third, Vietnam will accelerate infrastructure development, particularly in transport, ports, energy, and other essential facilities. It will also strengthen technological capabilities and links between domestic companies and foreign-invested enterprises. "Vietnam will attract investment selectively, with an emphasis on technology transfer and workforce training and development," Hung said. The remaining priorities are improving the quality and effectiveness of education and training, and strengthening foreign relations while diversifying partnerships to create more development opportunities. Maintaining strategic autonomy Mergenthaler also asked how Vietnam could maintain strategic autonomy amid declining international trust and intensifying competition among major powers. Hung said strategic autonomy meant building domestic capabilities to preserve the country's ability to make independent decisions and choose partnerships that serve national interests while respecting other countries' legitimate interests. Vietnam will focus on improving economic competitiveness, supporting domestic businesses, and advancing science, technology, and innovation. It will also safeguard national sovereignty and security, including energy, food, environmental, and human security, while diversifying essential supply chains to reduce exposure to external shocks. At the same time, Vietnam will pursue international integration and make effective use of its 18 signed free trade agreements to expand markets, diversify partners, and attract capital, technology, and knowledge. "Our goal is not only to participate more deeply in global value chains but also to strengthen domestic capabilities, gradually master technologies, and generate greater added value for the Vietnamese economy," Hung said. Vietnam's role in the global economy Asked about Vietnam's ambitions in the evolving global economic landscape through 2035, Hung said the country aims to become an emerging hub for digital technology, new and green energy, and green agriculture. picked.t: California Fitness closures leave members fearing loss of prepaid fees
picked.body: Bao Phuong, 40, paid VND104 million for a premium lifetime membership in August but managed to attend only about 10 workout sessions before her regular club in Ho Chi Minh City's Vuon Lai Ward announced a temporary closure. On Oct. 25, she was informed that the facility would suspend operations until Oct. 31 for restructuring. Members were advised to visit other branches, but the announcement did not identify any alternatives. After checking the chain's 14 locations in the region, Phuong found that only two were still operating, at Aeon Mall Binh Tan and Binh Duong Square, both far from her home. Her discounted Iconic membership promised lifetime access to all California Fitness & Yoga clubs, along with exclusive benefits including VIP lounges, swimming pools, reserved parking, wellness beverages and free towels. "I barely got through ten sessions. Now, when I try calling my sales rep or the customer care hotline, nobody answers the phone," she said. In Hanoi, Dang Le Anh Dung, 29, faced a similar situation after paying an additional VND20 million in late August to extend his membership until 2031. Dung had been exercising at the chain's Lang Ward branch since November 2024. However, shortly after renewing his membership, the club began reducing services. Fresh smoothies were replaced with bottled water in early September. By October, complimentary towels, workout clothes and drinking water had been discontinued, and the swimming pool was closed. The branch eventually shut down in mid-October. Dung moved to another location in Vinh Tuy Ward, but it also closed on Oct. 25. Two other branches in Hoan Kiem and Thanh Xuan stopped admitting members the following day. His sales representative apologized, saying she would never have encouraged him to renew had she known the company would face such difficulties. By Oct. 28, VnExpress had confirmed that all nine California Fitness & Yoga locations in Hanoi were closed. At the Hang Da and Royal City branches, security guards prevented customers from entering even though no official closure notices had been displayed. Clubs in Da Nang and Bien Hoa also suspended operations on Oct. 24-25. In Ho Chi Minh City, only the Aeon Mall Binh Tan location remained operational. The chain had operated approximately 35 clubs nationwide in 2025. Attempts by VnExpress to contact the company's hotline and managers in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City were unsuccessful. The manager of the Binh Tan branch declined to discuss plans for compensating affected members. CEO apologizes Amid mounting complaints, California Fitness & Yoga founder and CEO Dane Fort released an apology video on the company's verified social media account on Oct. 19, addressing members, employees and business partners. He promised to remove additional charges for certain group fitness and yoga classes, restore complimentary towels and drinking water, and cover parking fees for customers. Fort requested 30 days to reorganize the business and said the company would announce a solution for long-term memberships by Nov. 19. However, employees said the company's financial difficulties had been apparent for months. Quoc Binh, who worked as a sales consultant at a Hanoi branch for four years, said he and his colleagues had gone without salaries for five consecutive months beginning in June 2026. Despite repeated assurances from management, workers continued reporting to work in hopes of eventually receiving their wages. Some took additional jobs to cover living expenses. On Oct. 25, staff received notices placing them on unpaid leave. "The internal memo said we were pausing through Oct. 31 to reorganize, but none of us know if the doors will ever open again," Binh said. He added that customers who had spent hundreds of millions of dong on membership packages were calling employees in distress, but staff could offer little reassurance. California Fitness & Yoga sells four membership categories: Platinum, Premier, Iconic and Centuryon. Basic packages cost approximately VND500,000-700,000 per month when customers pay in advance for 18-24 months, while premium memberships can cost hundreds of millions of dong. The closures have created an additional financial burden for members who financed their packages through banks or installment payment providers. Because the fitness company received the membership fees upfront, customers remain obligated to repay their loans even when they cannot use the services. Missing repayments could damage their credit histories. As uncertainty over the chain's future grows, members have begun organizing to pursue possible legal action. Since Oct. 27, hundreds of customers have joined online groups to collect membership agreements, payment receipts, bank statements and other documents for potential joint complaints. picked.t: Chinese billionaire Zhang Zetian dazzles in Vietnamese designer's gown at Hong Kong gala
picked.body: Zhang wore a haute couture creation from Phan Huy's 2026–2027 collection to the event held at Hong Kong's M+ museum last weekend. Inspired by modern sculpture, the gown featured a distinctive architectural silhouette supported by an internal wire structure. Intricate crystal embellishments, meticulously attached by hand, added a subtle sparkle to the sculptural design. Fashion enthusiasts on Chinese social media platform Weibo praised Zhang for carrying off the unconventional design with elegance, noting that its complex shape can be challenging to wear. Her slender figure, minimal makeup and simple hairstyle were also credited with complementing the dramatic gown without overwhelming the overall look. The charity event brought together prominent figures from the business and entertainment worlds, including Pansy Ho and Laurinda Ho, daughters of the late Macau casino tycoon Stanley Ho, as well as Chow Yun-fat, his wife and actress Carina Lau. Zhang holds a senior leadership role at the e-commerce company founded by her husband, Liu Qiangdong. According to the 2025 Hurun rich list, the couple has a combined fortune of 58 billion yuan (US$8.6 billion). As an adviser to the company's fashion business, Zhang frequently attends major international fashion weeks and prestigious luxury events. Over the past year, she has also ventured into broadcasting, hosting an interview program featuring influential personalities from business and the arts. Zhang first became an internet celebrity in 2009 after a photograph of her holding a cup of milk tea went viral, earning her the nickname "Sister Milk Tea." In 2011, she gained direct admission to China's prestigious Tsinghua University. She later chose to focus on her education rather than pursue acting, declining an offer to star in renowned director Zhang Yimou's historical film "The Flowers of War." Phan Huy, 27, comes from Quang Tri Province in central Vietnam and is a guest member of the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode. His designs often draw inspiration from childhood memories of rural Vietnam, incorporating images of sunset landscapes, glowing fireflies, floating duckweed and lotus ponds under moonlight into contemporary haute couture creations.

picked.t: 비엣콤은행, 9월 기준 세전익 40조 동 돌파 전년동기比 22%↑…은행권 1위 유지
picked.body: (사진=비엣콤은행) 베트남 4대 국영상업은행 중 하나인 비엣콤은행(Vietcombank)이 9월까지 40조4,400억 동(15억6,720만여 달러)에 달하는 세전이익을 거두며 수익성 기준 은행권 1위를 지켰다. 다만 3분기 세전이익은 11조2,000억 동(4억3,400만여 달러)으로 제자리였는데, 이는 대손충당금을 1년 전의 8배까지 늘린 영향으로 풀이된다. 비엣콤은행이 최근 공시한 3분기 연결재무제표에 따르면, 3분기 세전이익은 11조2,000억 동을 기록했다. 지난해 같은 기간과 비교하면 유의미한 증감은 없었으나, 올 들어 9월 기준 누계 세전이익은 전년 동기 대비 22% 늘어난 40조4,400억 동을 기록했다. 베트남투자개발은행(BIDV)와 VP은행(VPBank), 테크콤은행(Techcombank) 등 주요 은행과 비교하면 약 10조 동(3억8,750만여 달러) 많은 규모다. 9월 말 기준 주요 수익원인 순이자수익은 약 57조2,000억 동(약 22억1,680만 달러)으로 전년 동기 대비 35% 증가했다. 이 외 외환 거래 수입이 6조4,000억 동(2억4,800만여 달러) 이상, 기타 영업수익이 5조9,000억 동(약 2억2,870만 달러) 이상으로 비이자수익도 성장세를 보였다. 같은 기간 총영업이익은 약 73조 동(약 28억2,910만 달러)으로 전년 동기 대비 37% 증가했다. 또한 충당금 적립을 늘리면서 대손충당금은 9조2,000억 동(3억5,650만여 달러)으로 4배 가까이 증가했다. 특히 3분기 대손충당금만 6조2,000억 동(약 2억4,030만 달러)을 쌓았는데, 이로 인해 호실적에도 분기 세전이익이 제자리 걸음했다. 9월 말 기준 총자산은 약 2,680조 동(1,038억6,180만 달러)으로 연초 대비 10% 가까이 늘었다. 대출잔액은 1,810조 동(약 701억4,550만 달러) 이상으로 8.5% 늘었고, 예금잔액은 약 1,780조 동(689억8,280만여 달러)으로 6.5% 늘었다. 채권 등 유가증권 발행액도 47조4,000억 동(약 18억3,700만 달러)으로 75% 급증했다. 부실채권(NPL) 비율은 올해 초 0.58%에서 3분기 말 0.71%로 상승했다.
